title: Svartsengi & Grindavík Magma Intrusion 2024
headline: Repeated magmatic dike intrusions lifted ground surface by +38 cm before fissure eruptions.
story: Along Iceland's Reykjanes volcanic belt, intense magmatic dike propagation and magma chamber inflation beneath the Svartsengi geothermal power plant drove extraordinary ground deformation throughout early 2024. InSAR interferograms captured rapid ground inflation of up to 1 cm per day, followed by sudden subsidence and fissure eruptions that endangered the town of Grindavík.
why_sar: Why radar sees through cloud and night: Arctic winter weather brings constant blizzards, cloud cover, and polar twilight; radar satellites reliably provide sub-centimeter displacement updates every few days.

story_steps.title: Svartsengi Geothermal Field Baseline
story_steps.description: Lava fields and infrastructure near Grindavík and the Blue Lagoon prior to unrest.

story_steps.title: Concentric Magma Inflation Fringes
story_steps.description: InSAR interference fringes show an elliptical dome centered on the Svartsengi magma reservoir 4-5 km deep.

story_steps.title: Grindavík Grabent Subsidence
story_steps.description: While Svartsengi inflated, the ground directly above the magma dike subsided over 1 meter inside Grindavík town.

story_steps.title: Protective Earthen Berm Defense
story_steps.description: InSAR deformation contours guided Icelandic civil defense engineers constructing giant defensive barriers.
